_comment: Editorial layer over the fleet register (https://loki.orangecat.ch/api/fleet/register). The register says WHAT EXISTS and WHERE; this file says how bitbaum presents it: the one-line `what`, the display `name`, `order` within a section, a `group` when the register's kind/status would file it wrongly (or to curate 'Not live'), and `extras` for things the register does not know. Keyed by canonical slug = repository name. A register row without a `what` here is not shown at all; a live row with one is filed by its kind.

sbb-fundbuero.name: Nordbahn Fundbüro
sbb-fundbuero.what: Lost on the train, while you are still on it.

extras.name: Annushka
extras.what: Painter, shown on a house address
extras._why: static site plus a dead :4030 api; does not fit an apps.conf row

_packages_comment: Editorial layer over the DERIVED package registry (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitbaum/fleet/main/registers/packages.json, generated by fleet's shared-registry audit from real package.json data across the org). The registry says WHICH packages exist, how many apps use each, and the install line; this file says how bitbaum describes them in one line. Keyed by package slug. No `what` here falls back to the package's own npm description, which is usually too long for a card.

ai-kit.what: Which model to call, whether the vendor still serves it, and what to do when every one of them fails.

mail-kit.what: One email layer for every app. Never throws — it returns whether the mail was sent.

bip-kit.what: Blog, roadmap and changelog from repo-authored markdown. Typed blocks, your design tokens on top.

ai-forms.what: Fill a form from prose, then refine it in conversation. Headless, so every app keeps its own look.

threadkit.what: Message threads where permission is participation — not a role column. An AI obeys the same rules as a person.

limitkit.what: Rate limiting as a decision, not middleware. Bounded memory by construction, standard headers.

listkit.what: A list as a query: facets, a URL you can share, sorting that puts missing values last. No markup.

sitekit.what: A website as data — a closed set of section shapes, validated, with per-field provenance.

design-tokens.what: One tokens.css behind three products, so a retheme is an edit to one file.
